findings.summary: The new left-boundary check treats ':' and '.' (and any run of slashes not preceded by file:) before a root as 'inside a name', so the net no longer rewrites a real host path glued to a colon or written after a non-file URL scheme or a '\\.\' device prefix; no test pins this exception
findings.scenario: A remote client's Error frame reading 'open:C:\proj\assets\a.txt' (Windows) or 'key:/srv/game/x' (POSIX) passes RedactHostPaths unchanged; only the net is affected (no current site found that builds such text: std::filesystem_error quotes or brackets its paths, every e.what() path to a remote client goes through ClientText::Failure)

findings.summary: Only single '\' is normalised: a host path whose separators are doubled (JSON- or C-escaped, 'C:\\proj\\assets') or URL-encoded is never matched by the net
findings.scenario: An error text that embeds a JSON dump or an escaped path normalises 'C:\\proj\\x' to 'C://proj//x', which does not contain 'C:/proj', so the folder reaches a remote client; pre-existing since 9b77519 and net-only

findings.summary: The 'net under the messages' paragraph was not updated for the delta: it still lists the working folder unconditionally (HostRoots now drops a drive/file-system root) and states only the right-hand 'matches whole' rule, not that a folder after a name char, ':', '.' or a slash run (other than file:// and \\?\) is left alone
findings.scenario: A reader trusting the docs assumes 'path:/srv/game/x' or a cwd of C:\ is rewritten for a remote client; the code leaves both as they are (testing.html was updated, this section was not)
